content.value_statement: API teams need accurate docs that match changing endpoints and examples. This skill helps Claude, Codex, and Claude Code create references, guides, and interactive documentation.
actual_capabilities: Generates API reference guides from OpenAPI or Swagger specifications.
Drafts getting started, authentication, error handling, rate limit, and pagination sections.
Creates request examples for curl, JavaScript, Python, Go, and Ruby.
Outlines Swagger UI, Redoc, Stoplight Elements, Docusaurus, Slate, ReadMe.io, and MkDocs workflows.
Prepares documentation exports such as Markdown, HTML, Postman collections, and SDK generation plans.
limitations: Does not verify that endpoints, schemas, or examples match a live service.
Interactive documentation setup may require project-specific dependencies and manual configuration.
Generated examples can include placeholders that must be replaced with real service values.
Does not securely manage API keys or publishing credentials.

use_cases.title: Document a New API
use_cases.description: Create reference pages, request examples, schemas, and status code notes from an OpenAPI specification.

use_cases.title: Prepare Developer Guides
use_cases.description: Turn endpoint details into getting started, authentication, error handling, pagination, and rate limit guides.

use_cases.title: Launch Interactive Docs
use_cases.description: Plan Swagger UI, Redoc, or Stoplight Elements documentation with sample requests and publishing steps.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Basic Reference
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner: start from an API specification.
prompt_templates.prompt: Generate an API reference for this OpenAPI specification. Include endpoints, parameters, schemas, responses, and clear request examples.

prompt_templates.title: Add Onboarding Guides
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate: expand reference docs into user guides.
prompt_templates.prompt: Create getting started, authentication, error handling, pagination, and rate limit documentation for this API reference.

prompt_templates.title: Build Interactive Docs
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced: plan an interactive documentation experience.
prompt_templates.prompt: Design an interactive documentation setup for this API. Compare Swagger UI, Redoc, and Stoplight Elements for this project.

prompt_templates.title: Plan Multi-Format Publishing
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced: prepare docs for several delivery channels.
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a publishing plan for Markdown, HTML, Postman collection, and SDK documentation outputs. Include validation and review steps.

output_examples.input: An OpenAPI specification for users, organizations, authentication, and billing endpoints.
output: Error, pagination, and rate limit sections.

output_examples.input: Existing code comments for a TypeScript or Python service.
output_examples.output: A structured draft with endpoint summaries, parameter descriptions, response notes, and missing documentation questions.

output_examples.input: A request to publish interactive docs for a developer portal.
output_examples.output: A setup plan comparing documentation tools, required assets, hosting steps, and review checks before release.

best_practices: Keep the OpenAPI specification as the source of truth and regenerate docs after API changes.
Replace placeholder tokens, domains, and examples before publishing.
Test every sample request against a staging environment before release.
anti_patterns: Publishing generated docs without checking authentication, error, and rate limit details.
Mixing real secrets into examples or screenshots.
Using interactive try-it-out features against production endpoints without limits.

faq.question: What inputs work best with this skill?
faq.answer: OpenAPI or Swagger files work best. Code comments, route lists, and existing docs can also provide useful structure.

faq.question: Can it create interactive documentation?
faq.answer: Yes. It can plan Swagger UI, Redoc, and Stoplight Elements setups with project-specific configuration notes.

faq.question: Does it verify live API behavior?
faq.answer: No. You should test generated examples against a staging service before publishing.

faq.question: Can it help with SDK documentation?
faq.answer: Yes. It can outline SDK generation steps and write usage docs for generated clients.

faq.question: Does it handle API keys safely?
faq.answer: It uses placeholders in examples. Do not paste real credentials into prompts, examples, or published docs.

faq.question: Will it run setup commands automatically?
faq.answer: No. It provides setup guidance. Users should approve and run project commands only when they choose.
